findings.title: Physical operation guard retires before actual native caller and its cleanup return
findings.source_facts: FINISH disarms timer at owner:382, sends CLOSED, and clears active. Frontend receive still executes _check/_pidfd/native proc IO and decoding/time checks; lease retire still runs after the disarm. Moreover actual native dispatch encloses ResultTool.handle in _run_with_activity_heartbeat, whose stop/join happens after handle/FINISH, and canonical result commit subsequently executes metadata callback, SessionDB flush and tool.completed UI callback. These are actual selected original native paths outside this guardian clock.
findings.counterexample: Complete output+observer while end is still ahead, issue FINISH, then delay frontend consumption/return or block original native metadata/DB/UI completion after handler returns. Guardian is idle with disarmed timer; same original call's tail can exceed end or remain active. If CLOSED arrives after end, receive rejects and ResultTool.handle emits its fallback JSON outside the retired guard. No source mechanism retains a physical guard through that tail.
findings.required_change: Move final guard custody/retirement to the real native operation terminal boundary and cover all owned native callback, result/session publication and cleanup paths under the original clock. A pre-return CLOSED ACK or post-check alone is insufficient; preserve the original frontend and native identities.
meaningful_controls: Actual blocked post-FINISH/pre-caller-return native path, including a delayed CLOSED consumption; record retained exact product pidfds and effective outside guard until actual return
Actual blocked native tool-result metadata callback / SessionDB flush / tool.completed UI after ResultTool.handle; original elapsed end includes this tail and adverse custody remains held
Positive direct/wrapped return and second distinct operation retain the same original frontend, AppSession and guardian; no borrowed previous result

findings.title: Sequence changes scope but does not prevent renewing one native operation
findings.source_facts: After FINISH active becomes None. Next ARM accepts any valid same original_ids with a later started_m and fresh end<=start+30; only sequence increments. No consumed native five-ID operation set or original operation clock is retained. Native _authorized_dispatch's once check protects one dispatch-state callback only, not a later state with the same native identities.
findings.counterexample: Authenticated original frontend sends ARM(I,S,E), completes FINISH, then ARM(I,S2,E2) with identical all five IDs and E2=S2+30. The reviewed state machine accepts this as a new scope. A different scope hash is not proof of a distinct original tool invocation.
findings.required_change: Bind one start/end/scope and terminal state to each genuine original native operation identity; reject a replay/renewal of the same invocation across FINISH and retain consumed identity state without a retry/reset. Prove genuine distinct later calls through the actual native producer.
meaningful_controls: Same actual native five IDs replayed after a successful FINISH; must not ARM a renewed +30
Duplicate original native call identity across separate dispatch states, not only two simultaneous ARM packets
Positive later genuine different tool_call_id/API operation on the same frontend with its own original<=30 clock

findings.title: Observer acquisition failures and adverse shutdown drop unreaped native custody
findings.source_facts: After fork, right.close and pidfd_open run before self.observer is assigned; either failure leaves no registered child in _stop_exact. Timeout/error only sends SIGKILL to retained pidfds; it performs no observer raw wait or durable custody handoff. run_one then raises/returns and guardian entry finally closes frontend/timer descriptors and exits. Bootstrap waits only its guardian child. Normal positive direct observer wait is present at :265, but adverse observer cleanup and the fork acquisition gap are not closed.
findings.counterexample: Actual fork succeeds, then pidfd_open (or parent socket close) fails. Child waits for GO/end and is not retained in owner.observer; guardian kills frontend and exits without exact child reap. Separately an owned observer stuck in a native uninterruptible IO path receives SIGKILL but can outlive guardian exit, whose retained pidfd is then lost. Correct refusal/UNKNOWN is not physical cleanup.
findings.required_change: Make direct-child acquisition exception safe before every child effect and preserve exact birth/pidfd/custody through adverse stop and exact raw join, or hand off authenticated retained custody to an already admitted outside native owner until closure. Do not release on signal request, EOF, dropped handles or guardian exit; no retry/wildcard target.
meaningful_controls: Real child spawned with pidfd allocation failure before GO and parent right.close failure; record its exact birth and actual reap/custody outcome
Owned sampler and settle observer failure, timeout, EOF/nonzero/close ambiguity; no orphan observer or forgotten descriptor
Uninterruptible observer control remains STOP_UNCONFIRMED/red with exact custody retained; wrapper exit or absence never substitutes for raw/effects closure

findings.title: Actual AppSession identity is not retained or checked
findings.source_facts: ClassicConsoleOutput retains Application/Console/stream/cap but no actual AppSession. _RendererSession ignores the AppSession returned by session.__enter__. write_renderer_envelope copies the current Context and set_app(app) mutates whichever AppSession that context holds; native current.py confirms this behavior. Lease checks only app.input.fileno()==0, application/output references and wrapper.app_session.app, not get_app_session() identity or original Input object. Reader checks CLI/cap/output only.
findings.counterexample: Enter a distinct copied AppSession containing the same original input/output/Application while keeping original _TURN/_TOOL/cap/Console references. Existing checks still pass, and the queued renderer task uses that different session. The named copied_AppSession negative has no corresponding identity enforcement.
findings.required_change: Capture the actual native AppSession and Input at the original session/Application producer and require exact object identity in admission, cross-thread/native renderer dispatch, restoration, live reader and final cleanup. Carry existing opaque context/capabilities without reconstructing or replacing the UI.
meaningful_controls: Actual distinct AppSession with same input/output/Application references, and a copied contextual AppSession in the native worker/renderer callback; refuse before effects
Original Input object substitution with an equal numeric fd/OFD; must not be accepted as the same original input
Positive direct/wrapped operation keeps the actual original AppSession/Application/Console/stream/PluginContext/CLIUserScope references at every boundary

findings.title: Observer durable state witness does not close named-inode replacement during fsync
findings.source_facts: _read_private_at snapshots and re-fstats the opened fd before fsync, then fsyncs and closes it. It never compares the current directory entry to the observed fd, and does not revalidate after the fsync barrier. Later directory fsync can concern a replacement state.json while the returned bytes belong to the old inode. The artifact read implementation does check its named entry; the new observer does not.
findings.counterexample: After z=fstat(fd) passes, block actual observer fsync and replace state.json by a new private inode. Resume fsync; the old fd bytes are accepted and directory fsync completes for the current namespace. An equivalent copied valid proposal in the later current row can match its certificate even though the actual stable named inode control changed during observation. This contradicts the named state_inode_changed_during_observe negative.
findings.required_change: Bind directory/name and file generation across the actual durable observation and fsync/close boundary, and ensure caller projection consumes that exact current authoritative generation. Refuse any ambiguous substitution rather than inferring from old fd stability alone.
meaningful_controls: Real state.json replacement after final pre-fsync fstat, during native fsync and before directory fsync, including same-content replacement; no certified delivery for the changed named inode
Retained record directory replacement and symlink/foreign native state control with live current-row binding
Unchanged exact private named inode positive, actual file and directory barriers, direct observer raw wait and final caller read all bound
